to race over 1,500 metres in Barcelona.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-56) In her first race since the World Cross Country, Radcliffe finished 11th.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-57) At the London Grand Prix, Radcliffe finished second, one second outside of her British record, in only her second track race of the season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-58) At the [Weltklasse Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse_Z%C3%BCrich "Weltklasse Zürich")[IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") meeting Radcliffe competed in the 3,000 metres and finished in fourth place.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-59) At the UK trials won the 5,000 metres title.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-60) The [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Grand_Prix_(athletics) "British Grand Prix (athletics)") saw Radcliffe race over 3000 metres, where once again she finished third.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-61) At the [2000 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, Radcliffe finished sixth in her 10,000 metres heat to qualify for the final.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-62) In the final Radcliffe set a new British record,

but crossed the line in fourth and was highly disappointed to miss out on a medal.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-63) Radcliffe returned to action by winning the BUPA Ireland five-mile race.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-64) At the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run"), Radcliffe ran a new European record for the half marathon, as she won the race in a time of 67 minutes and 7 seconds.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-65) Radcliffe was then selected for the [2000 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2000 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") in Mexico.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-66) Radcliffe won her first World title, despite suffering a panic attack when her nose tape, designed to help her breathe, fell off halfway round.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-67) The good run of form came to an end, when she turned her attention to the Cross Country events and finished third in Brussels.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-68) Radcliffe confirmed that her last race of the year would be the [Great North Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Cross_Country "Great North Cross Country").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-69) There Radcliffe defeated Tulu by seventy-five seconds,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-70) in eight inches of snow.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-71)

She won back-to-back titles in the 2000 and 2001 [IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"), winning a third title in 2003.
